haiku-low.q1: They see the generic 200 message, "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no mail is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The fourth request is rolled back. The user gets the same generic message, and nothing is written or sent.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes after creation. Issuing a newer link, or using the link to reset, ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live and unused. The form returns with the error, nothing is written, and the link works until expires_at.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in. All sessions rows for that user are deleted, including the current device. The user is redirected to /login and signs in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The sender retries with backoff up to 3 more times, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told; they can request again.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory and put in the queued job and email link (https://app/reset?token=raw). Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: The API SHA-256 hashes the token and selects the reset row with matching token_hash. It must exist, have used_at null, and have a future expires_at.
haiku-low.q9: In the pw_reset table, counting that user's rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes, dead ones included. Old rows drop out once they age past 60 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: All of the account's still-live tokens get used_at set to now() inside the same transaction as the new insert, before COMMIT. They are stamped, not deleted.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: used_at is stamped, users.password_hash is updated, and the user's sessions rows are deleted, then COMMIT. The confirmation email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The reset UPDATE has WHERE id AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). If it touches 0 rows, the transaction rolls back, so only one submit succeeds.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message as always: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no mail is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of this user's pw_reset rows created in the last 60 min is already 3 or more, so the transaction ROLLBACKs. The user still gets the (*1) 200 message, and nothing is written or sent.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if it is used (used_at stamped on a successful reset), or if a newer link is requested for the account (older live tokens get used_at = now()).
sonnet.q4: Still live and unused. Nothing is written, the form comes back with the error, and the link keeps working until expires_at.
sonnet.q5: None. All of the user's session rows are deleted, including the device they reset from. They are redirected to /login and sign in with the new password, because no session is created.
sonnet.q6: The sender retries with backoff up to 3 more times, then logs and drops the job. The user is not notified. They can ask again.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated (32 random bytes) in API memory and put into the queued job as the link https://app/reset?token=<raw>. The job goes on the queue after the (*7) transaction commits and before the (*1) response. The sender then mails it. Only the hash goes into the DB.
sonnet.q8: The API hashes the ?token value with SHA-256 and selects the reset record whose token_hash matches. The record must exist, have used_at null and have an expires_at in the future. Otherwise the user gets the "This link has expired, request a new one" page.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. It is the pw_reset table itself, counting the user's rows with created_at in the last 60 min, including dead (stamped) ones. Old requests drop out when their created_at is more than 60 min old. Rows are stamped used_at, not deleted.
sonnet.q10: The older links are not deleted. The user's still-live tokens get used_at = now(), in the same transaction (*7) as the new insert. This happens after the rate-limit count and after the code is generated, and before the new row is inserted and COMMIT.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the reset record's used_at is stamped, users.password_hash is updated, and all of that user's sessions rows are deleted, then COMMIT. The "password changed" mail is enqueued only after that COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The UPDATE sets used_at with WHERE id = row AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). Whichever submit gets there first stamps it. The other touches 0 rows, ROLLBACKs and gets the expired page, so only one changes the password.
